analyst_view.overall: Early view: Third against fourth, one point apart. Freiburg have their best-scoring start in club history under Julian Schuster and have conceded only ten, while Leipzig have won every home game but taken only three points away. Both clubs play in Europe that week (Freiburg in the Conference League, Leipzig in the Champions League), so rotation is likely.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.4 goals. I lean slightly higher: Leipzig's league games have produced 40 goals in nine (joint-most in the league) and Freiburg have scored 20, a club record at this stage. Leipzig's poor away form has included a 6-1 defeat at Bayern, so their trips have not been low-scoring affairs.

corners.text: The site expects 8.8 corners. I lean higher: Freiburg had around two thirds of the ball against Union and rely a lot on Niklas Beste's and Vincenzo Grifo's deliveries, while Leipzig's wide players Antonio Nusa and Brajan Gruda attack defenders one against one.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.3 cards. Freiburg usually take two or three bookings and Leipzig have been fairly clean (one booking against Augsburg), so I stay with the number.

shots.text: The site has 26.2 shots. Two attacking sides near the top, with Freiburg dominating the ball at home and Leipzig shooting often, point to slightly more than the number, so I lean higher.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.8 on target. Rotation after European games could blunt both attacks, which balances my higher shot view, so I keep this close to the number.
